title: Timestamp Trouble Simulator
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Run identical readings through four timestamp formats and a daylight saving transition, and judge which failures can be repaired and which destroyed the information for good.

learningObjectives: Critique four timestamp formats against the same logged data.
Judge which failures are recoverable and which permanently destroy information.
prerequisites: Knowing what a time zone is
Chapter 5 sections on why the station needs a clock

keyQuestions: Two readings share a timestamp. What exactly has been lost?
Why does a missing hour look like a hardware fault?
What property of ISO 8601 makes an alphabetical sort come out chronological?
commonMisconceptions: Believing a time zone abbreviation is enough to disambiguate a repeated hour.
Assuming any timestamp problem can be fixed in post-processing.
Treating "use UTC" as a style preference rather than a data integrity requirement.
assessmentOpportunities: Distinguishes a recoverable timestamp failure from an unrecoverable one and defends the distinction.
Explains why ISO 8601 sorts correctly as plain text.
Argues for UTC from a demonstrated consequence rather than from authority.
